 10|## Overview
 11|
 12|These principles govern the design, implementation, and operation of the SovereignAI system. They serve as the foundation for architectural decisions, development practices, and operational procedures. All agents and developers should reference these principles when making decisions about system changes or implementations.
 13|
 14|## Core Architecture Principles (CA)
 15|
 16|### CA-1. Core is Sacred
 17|**Rule**: The system has exactly 12 core modules. All other functionality must be pluggable.
 18|**Implementation**: Core modules provide essential system services. Any feature outside the core must be implemented as a pluggable component.
 19|**Agent Guidance**: When adding new functionality, always implement as a pluggable component rather than modifying core modules.
 20|
 21|### CA-2. Everything Pluggable
 22|**Rule**: All components are equal and interchangeable: adapters, skills, memory backends, models, UIs.
 23|**Implementation**: Use consistent interfaces and dependency injection. No component should have special privileges or hardcoded dependencies.
 24|**Agent Guidance**: Design new components with standardized interfaces that can be swapped without affecting system operation.
 25|
 26|### CA-3. No Provider Lock-in
 27|**Rule**: System must continue operating if any single component is removed.
 28|**Implementation**: Design for graceful degradation. Components should be hot-swappable without system restart.
 29|**Agent Guidance**: Never create hard dependencies on specific providers. Always allow alternative implementations.
 30|
 31|### CA-4. Local-First
 32|**Rule**: System runs fully offline. Cloud services are optional enhancements, not requirements.
 33|**Implementation**: All core functionality must work without internet connectivity. Cloud features are opt-in escalations.
 34|**Scope**: v1 supports Windows only.
 35|**Agent Guidance**: Implement offline-first. Cloud features should be optional add-ons, not core dependencies.
 36|
 37|### CA-5. Wire as You Go
 38|**Rule**: No speculative contracts or empty placeholder directories.
 39|**Implementation**: Create components only when needed. Avoid premature abstraction or framework code.
 40|**Agent Guidance**: Implement concrete functionality first. Add abstractions only when multiple implementations exist.
 41|
 42|### CA-6. One User, One System
 43|**Rule**: Single user system accessible from anywhere. All UIs connect to the same core.
 44|**Implementation**: Core is user-scoped. Multiple UI clients can connect to the same user's core instance.
 45|**Deferred**: Phone/relay support.
 46|**Agent Guidance**: Design for single-user multi-device access. Core state is per-user, not shared across users.
 47|
 48|### CA-7. Modular Over Simple
 49|**Rule**: Prefer modular, flexible design over simple, monolithic approaches.
 50|**Implementation**: Components should fail independently. System degradation should be graceful, not catastrophic.
 51|**Agent Guidance**: Design for failure isolation. When one component fails, others should continue operating.
 52|
 53|### CA-8. UI Process Separation
 54|**Rule**: UIs are separate processes consuming the capability API via a standardized interface.
 55|**Implementation**: 10-section sidebar structure: Orchestrator, Workers, Tasks, Skills, Memory, Models, Adapters, Hardware, Logs, Options.
 56|**Agent Guidance**: UI components must communicate via API. No direct core access from UI processes.
 57|
 58|### CA-9. Observability by Default
 59|**Rule**: No silent failures. All traces must be logged locally via TraceEmitter.
 60|**Implementation**: Every operation must emit trace data. Failures must be visible and actionable.
 61|**Agent Guidance**: Add trace emission to all new operations. Ensure failure modes are observable.
 62|
 63|### CA-10. Dependency Injection Only
 64|**Rule**: No global state or context bags. Maximum 15 constructor arguments per component.
 65|**Implementation**: Use constructor injection for all dependencies. Avoid static state or global variables.
 66|**Agent Guidance**: Pass dependencies explicitly via constructors. Keep constructor signatures focused.
 67|
 68|### CA-11. Strong and Robust
 69|**Rule**: Fail gracefully, isolate faults, recover without manual intervention.
 70|**Implementation**: Implement fault isolation, automatic recovery, and graceful degradation patterns.
 71|**Agent Guidance**: Design for failure scenarios. Implement automatic recovery where possible.
 72|
 73|## Development Principles (DP)
 74|
 75|### DP-1. Test-File Creation
 76|**Rule**: Every code file must have accompanying test files created simultaneously.
 77|**Implementation**: When creating implementation files, immediately create corresponding test files with initial test structure.
 78|**Agent Guidance**: Never create implementation files without test files. Test structure should mirror implementation structure.
 79|
 80|### DP-2. Modular Functionality
 81|**Rule**: Functions must be modular so that updates to one function don't break others.
 82|**Implementation**: Follow single responsibility principle. Minimize coupling between functions. Use clear interfaces.
 83|**Agent Guidance**: Design functions to be independent. Changes to one function should not require changes to others.
 84|
 85|### DP-3. Best Practices Compliance
 86|**Rule**: All code must follow established best practices for the language and framework.
 87|**Implementation**: Reference project-specific style guides and industry standards. Use linting and formatting tools.
 88|**Agent Guidance**: Check existing code patterns before implementing new code. Follow established conventions.
 89|
 90|### DP-4. Internal Implementation
 91|**Rule**: Create functionality internally rather than relying on external programs.
 92|**Implementation**: Prefer native implementation over shell commands or external process execution.
 93|**Agent Guidance**: Implement functionality directly in the codebase rather than calling external programs.
 94|
 95|## Operational Principles (OP)
 96|
 97|### OP-1. Comprehensive Logging
 98|**Rule**: Everything within execution must be logged and categorized.
 99|**Implementation**: Use structured logging with consistent categories. All operations must emit log events.
100|**Agent Guidance**: Add logging to all operations. Use standardized log categories for consistency.
101|
102|### OP-2. Best Practices Enforcement
103|**Rule**: Application must ensure best practices are followed for all components.
104|**Implementation**: Implement validation and compliance checking. Use automated tools where possible.
105|**Agent Guidance**: Include validation logic in the application layer. Prevent non-compliant code from executing.
106|
107|## Deferred Principles (DF)
108|
109|### DF-1. Security via Reasoning
110|**Rule**: Security Guard is a user-invoked tool, not an automatic gate.
111|**Status**: Deferred for future implementation.
112|**Implementation**: Security analysis should be available on-demand, not blocking normal operations.
113|
114|### DF-2. Provenance Enforcement
115|**Rule**: External components must have verifiable provenance.
116|**Status**: Deferred for future implementation.
117|**Implementation**: Implement component signing and verification for external plugins and extensions.

 18|## Core Workflow Commands
 19|
 20|### **SCAN**
 21|**Definition**: Examine all documents within scope line by line without skipping anything - comprehensive examination required for governance compliance.
 22|
 23|**Usage**: Used when comprehensive examination of documents is required for governance compliance, quality assurance, or consistency verification. This is the primary scanning method and cannot be replaced by pattern matching tools like grep.

 25|**Examples**:
 26|- **SCAN** all harness architecture files for consistency checks
 27|- **SCAN** App/ directory line by line for compliance verification
 28|- **SCAN** workflow files to validate template compliance

 31|
 32|### **PRINT**
 33|**Definition**: Output text to chat interface for user visibility (not to files or logs).
 34|
 35|**Usage**: Used to communicate workflow status, progress updates, and important information to the user during workflow execution. This command does not write to files or logs.
 36|
 37|**Examples**:
 38|- **PRINT** "Workflow initialization complete"
 39|- **PRINT** "Scan strategy selected - Full Comprehensive"
 40|- **PRINT** "Consistency check complete - 0 issues found"

 44|### **VALIDATION**
 45|**Definition**: Validate step completion before proceeding to next phase.
 46|
 47|**Usage**: Used to ensure that workflow steps have completed successfully and meet quality criteria before moving to the next phase. This is a quality validation mechanism.
 48|
 49|**Examples**:
 50|- **VALIDATION**: Validate file reference extraction completed successfully
 51|- **VALIDATION**: Validate workflow structure check completed successfully
 52|- **VALIDATION**: Validate that all referenced files exist
 53|
 54|---
 55|
 56|### **STATUS TRACKING**
 57|**Definition**: Update workflow status for monitoring and recovery.
 58|
 59|**Usage**: Used to track workflow progress, enable recovery from failures, and provide visibility into workflow execution state. Status updates are typically written to workflow_state.json or similar tracking mechanisms.
 60|
 61|**Examples**:
 62|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 63|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_in_progress"
 64|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
 65|
 66|---
 67|
 68|### **TERMINATE**
 69|**Definition**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1).
 70|
 71|**Usage**: Used in single-execution workflows to signal completion and prevent automatic looping. This is the workflow termination command for utility workflows.
 72|
 73|**Examples**:
 74|- **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)
 75|- **TERMINATE**: Workflow execution complete - workflow terminated
 76|
 77|---
 78|
 79|## Workflow-Specific Commands
 80|
 81|### **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**
 82|**Definition**: Apply execution mode handling patterns based on selected mode (Manual/Auto/Complete).
 83|
 84|**Usage**: Used to determine how the workflow should respond to failures based on the user-selected execution mode.
 85|
 86|**Modes**:
 87|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight
 88|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures (auto-stop on errors)
 89|- **Complete**: Continue past failures (ignore all errors)
 90|
 91|**Examples**:
 92|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns
 93|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply review mode handling patterns
 94|
 95|---
 96|
 97|### **MANUAL**
 98|**Definition**: Agent explains exactly what they want to do, then user has choice Yes, No, Other.
 99|
100|**Usage**: Used when complete user oversight is required throughout the workflow process. The agent must explain their intended actions clearly and get explicit user approval before proceeding.
101|
102|**Examples**:
103|- **MANUAL**: Agent explains proposed action and user chooses Yes/No/Other
104|- **MANUAL**: User maintains full control and intervention throughout entire workflow
105|
106|---
107|
108|### **AUTOMATIC**
109|**Definition**: Process automatically until a failure and ask user how to proceed.
110|
111|**Usage**: Used when automated processing is desired but human intervention is needed at failure points. The workflow proceeds automatically but stops when failures occur to request user guidance on recovery.
112|
113|**Examples**:
114|- **AUTOMATIC**: Process automatically without user confirmation until failure
115|- **AUTOMATIC**: Stop at failures and ask user how to proceed with recovery
116|
117|---
118|
119|### **CONVERGENCE CHECK**
120|**Definition**: Verify panelist scores against quality thresholds.
121|
122|**Usage**: Used in Round Table review processes to determine if panelists have reached agreement on quality assessments.
123|
124|**Thresholds**:
125|- Clean pass: â‰¥4.5 score
126|- Acceptable pass: 3.5-4.4 score with documented rationale
127|- Fail: <3.5 score
128|
129|**Examples**:
130|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Check if all panelists chose PASS (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
131|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Verify convergence criteria met
132|
133|---
134|
135|### **QUOTA AWARENESS**
136|**Definition**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage for recovery tracking.
137|
138|**Usage**: Used to track subagent resource consumption and enable recovery if quota limits are approached or exceeded.
139|
140|**Examples**:
141|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage and track step progress
142|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Track quota usage for recovery if needed
143|
144|---
145|
146|### **LOOP DECISION**
147|**Definition**: Determine workflow continuation based on conditions.
148|
149|**Usage**: Used to control workflow flow and determine whether to loop back to previous phases or proceed forward.
150|
151|**Examples**:
152|- **LOOP DECISION**: If more plan steps remain â†’ Return to step 25 with next step
153|- **LOOP BACK**: Return to Phase 4 for next iteration
154|
155|---
156|
157|### **LOOP BACK**
158|**Definition**: Return to a previous workflow phase for iteration.
159|
160|**Usage**: Used when iterative refinement is required, typically when findings need to be applied and a process repeated.
161|
162|**Examples**:
163|- **LOOP BACK**: Return to Phase 4 for next iteration
164|- **LOOP BACK**: Return to Phase 6 for review material creation with revised plans
165|
166|---
167|
168|### **DELETE**
169|**Definition**: Remove specified files from the filesystem.
170|
171|**Usage**: Used to clean up outdated files, remove old revisions, or manage file lifecycle during workflow execution.
172|
173|**Examples**:
174|- **DELETE**: older plan revision files (Plans/Queued/plan-{N}.Rev{N-1}.md)
175|- **DELETE**: older batch prompt file immediately after new version creation
176|
177|---
178|
179|### **HANDOFF VALIDATION**
180|**Definition**: Verify handoff file integrity and completeness.
181|
182|**Usage**: Used when transferring work between agents to ensure all required information is present and accessible.
183|
184|**Examples**:
185|- **HANDOFF VALIDATION**: Verify handoff file integrity per template requirements
186|- **HANDOFF VALIDATION**: Validate all required fields are present
187|
188|---
189|
190|### **OPEN**
191|**Definition**: Open or load a skill/file for use in workflow execution.
192|
193|**Usage**: Used when accessing a skill or file to begin workflow operations.
194|
195|**Examples**:
196|- **OPEN** WorkflowOpen skill to dynamically load agent-specific rules
197|- **OPEN** configuration file for workflow initialization
198|
199|---
200|
201|### **ACTION**
202|**Definition**: Perform a specific action or operation as defined in workflow context.
203|
204|**Usage**: Used to indicate when an agent should execute a specific operation.
205|
206|**Examples**:
207|- **ACTION**: BP? - "workflow design best practices"
208|- **ACTION**: FC? - "accuracy and factual correctness verification"
209|
210|---
211|
212|### **CHECK**
213|**Definition**: Verify a condition or validate a requirement before proceeding.
214|
215|**Usage**: Used to ensure validation conditions are met before workflow progression.
216|
217|**Examples**:
218|- **CHECK**: All referenced documents exist
219|- **CHECK**: Workflow follows template structure
220|
221|---
222|
223|### **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**
224|**Definition**: Marker for mandatory steps that must be completed for workflow success.
225|
226|**Usage**: Used to highlight steps that are essential for workflow execution and cannot be skipped.
227|
228|**Examples**:
229|- **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**: Before any file creation, perform BP web search
230|- **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**: Document BP research findings and apply to implementation
231|

233|
234|## Decision and Planning Commands
235|
236|### **ARCHITECT OPINION**
237|**Definition**: Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection.
238|
239|**Usage**: Used by Architect agent to provide expert analysis and recommendations when presenting implementation options to users.
240|
241|**Examples**:
242|- **ARCHITECT OPINION**: Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection
243|- **ARCHITECT OPINION**: Recommend optimal approach based on analysis
244|
245|---
246|
247|### **PRESENTATION PATTERN**
248|**Definition**: Present options with metrics, provide architect opinion, use popup menu for selection.
249|
250|**Usage**: Used to standardize how options are presented to users, ensuring consistent format and decision-making process.
251|
252|**Examples**:
253|- **PRESENTATION PATTERN**: Present options with metrics, provide architect opinion, use popup menu
254|- **PRESENTATION PATTERN**: Use popup menu for selection
255|
256|---
257|
258|### **RULE ENFORCEMENT**
259|**Definition**: Ensure options comply with agent rules.
260|
261|**Usage**: Used to validate that proposed options or approaches comply with the relevant agent's governance rules.
262|
263|**Examples**:
264|- **RULE ENFORCEMENT**: Ensure options comply with Architect rules
265|- **RULE ENFORCEMENT**: Validate compliance with governance constraints
266|
267|---
268|
269|### **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**
270|**Definition**: Ask user to confirm specification or request modifications using popup menu.
271|
272|**Usage**: Used to get user approval on detailed specifications before proceeding with implementation.
273|
274|**Examples**:
275|- **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**: Ask user to confirm specification or request modifications
276|- **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**: Use popup menu with [Confirm/Modify] options
277|
278|---
279|
280|### **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**
281|**Definition**: Ask user to choose implementation mode using popup menu.
282|
283|**Usage**: Used to determine whether implementation should be automated or manual based on user preference.
284|
285|**Examples**:
286|- **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**: Ask user to choose using popup menu
287|- **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**: Select automated vs manual implementation
288|
289|---
290|
291|## Information and Notes
292|
293|### **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**
294|**Definition**: Validation system behavior notes for context.
295|
296|**Usage**: Used to provide explanatory notes about how the validation system behaves in specific situations.
297|
298|**Examples**:
299|- **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**: The validation system allows state-mutating tools automatically during this step
300|- **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**: User confirmation requests use ask_user_question for approval without triggering failure intervention
301|
302|---
303|
304|### **IMPORTANT**
305|**Definition**: Important notes that require attention but are not critical failures.
306|
307|**Usage**: Used to highlight important information that users should be aware of during workflow execution.
308|
309|**Examples**:
310|- **IMPORTANT**: Real-world testing required to avoid fake passes from isolated testing
311|- **IMPORTANT**: Hook file changes require Devin CLI restart
312|
313|---
314|
315|## Severity and Priority Markers
316|
317|### **CRITICAL**
318|**Definition**: Critical issues or required actions that must be addressed immediately.
319|
320|**Usage**: Used to mark issues that require immediate attention or actions that are mandatory for workflow success.
321|
322|**Examples**:
323|- **CRITICAL**: Violations that must be fixed (missing tests, hardcoded dependencies)
324|- **CRITICAL**: Hook file changes require Devin CLI restart before testing
325|
326|---
327|
328|### **HIGH**
329|**Definition**: High priority issues that should be addressed soon.
330|
331|**Usage**: Used to mark significant issues that should be resolved but are not immediately blocking.
332|
333|**Examples**:
334|- **HIGH**: Major quality issues that should be fixed (monolithic functions, poor modularity)
335|- **HIGH**: High priority issues requiring attention
336|
337|---
338|
339|### **MEDIUM**
340|**Definition**: Medium priority issues for improvement.
341|
342|**Usage**: Used to mark issues that represent improvements but are not urgent.
343|
344|**Examples**:
345|- **MEDIUM**: Best practices improvements (code readability, maintainability)
346|- **MEDIUM**: Medium priority issues for improvement
347|
348|---
349|
350|### **LOW**
351|**Definition**: Low priority minor suggestions.
352|
353|**Usage**: Used to mark minor suggestions or improvements that are optional.
354|
355|**Examples**:
356|- **LOW**: Minor suggestions (comments, formatting)
357|- **LOW**: Low priority issues for consideration
358|
359|---
360|
361|## Governance Terms
362|
363|### **BP** (Best Practice)
364|**Definition**: Established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding with major decisions.
365|
366|**Usage**: Used to indicate when web search for current best practices is required before making architectural or implementation decisions.
367|
368|**Examples**:
369|- **BP**: Web search for best practices before major architectural decisions
370|- **BP**: Research industry standards before implementation
371|
372|**Implementation**: When user input is "BP?" (Best Practice?), perform web search for current best practices relevant to the task at hand.
373|
374|---
375|
376|### **FC** (Fact Check)
377|**Definition**: Verification of factual accuracy for statements, claims, or technical assertions through research and validation.
378|
379|**Usage**: Used to indicate when verification of factual accuracy is required for user statements, agent assertions, or technical claims. Complements BP (Best Practice) research by ensuring factual correctness of specific statements.
380|
381|**Examples**:
382|- **FC**: Verify factual accuracy of technical claims before proceeding
383|- **FC**: Research and validate specific assertions or statements
384|- **FC**: Cross-check user statements or agent assumptions for factual correctness
385|
386|**Implementation**: When indicated by **FC?** (Fact Check?), perform targeted research to verify the factual accuracy of specific statements, claims, or technical assertions. This is distinct from **BP?** which focuses on best practices and industry standards.
387|
388|---
389|
390|### **SSOT** (Single Source of Truth)
391|**Definition**: Centralized repository for authoritative information that eliminates duplication and inconsistencies.
392|
393|**Usage**: Used to indicate the authoritative source for specific information, ensuring all agents reference the same accurate data.
394|
395|**Examples**:
396|- **SSOT**: Workflow/Terminology_Glossary.md is the SSOT for terminology definitions
397|- **SSOT**: STRUCTURE.md is the SSOT for directory structure information
398|
399|**Best Practice**: Establish SSOT for critical information to prevent inconsistencies and ensure all stakeholders work from the same data.
400|
401|---
402|
403|## Standard Terms
404|
405|### **ID**
406|**Definition**: Unique identifier for workflows, documents, or entities.
407|
408|**Usage**: Used to provide unique identification for workflows, documents, and other entities within the harness architecture.
409|
410|**Examples**:
411|- **ID**: WF-ARCH-001
412|- **ID**: WF-PLAN-001
413|
414|---
415|
416|### **DO**
417|**Definition**: Required actions that must be performed according to rules.
418|
419|**Usage**: Used in rule files to specify mandatory actions that agents must perform.
420|
421|**Examples**:
422|- **DO**: Verify each function follows single responsibility principle
423|- **DO**: Check that functions have clear inputs and outputs
424|
425|---
426|
427|## Terminology Governance
428|
429|### Glossary Maintenance
430|- **Owner**: Architect Agent
431|- **Update Process**: Architect agent reviews and updates glossary based on new terminology needs
432|- **Version Control**: All changes tracked with version history
433|- **Approval**: Architect agent approval required for new terms or definition changes
434|
435|### Term Addition Process
436|1. Identify new terminology need from workflow or rule updates
437|2. Research standard definitions and best practices
438|3. Draft definition with clear usage examples
439|4. Add to appropriate section in glossary
440|5. Update AGENTS.md to reference glossary if needed
441|6. Update workflows to reference new terms via glossary
442|
443|### Reference Pattern
444|All workflows and rules should reference this glossary for terminology understanding:
445|```markdown
446|For definition of **{TERM}**, see Workflow/Terminology_Glossary.md
447|```
448|
449|---
450|
451|## Best Practices for Terminology Usage
452|
453|1. **Consistency**: Always use terminology as defined in this glossary
454|2. **Reference**: When introducing new terms, reference this glossary
455|3. **Clarity**: Use defined terms consistently across all harness documents
456|4. **Updates**: Propagate terminology changes through Architect agent
457|5. **SSOT**: This glossary is the single source of truth for all terminology
458|

# Comprehensive Harness Analysis and Continuous Improvement System

## Objective
Conduct a thorough analysis of the SovereignAI project to identify and implement improvements that enhance:
1. Code Quality (maintainability, readability, best practices)
2. Rule Adherence (governance compliance, architectural principles)
3. Harness Efficiency (performance, token optimization, workflow effectiveness)

## Phase 1: Comprehensive Project Scan

### 1.1 Codebase Structure Analysis
- Map the entire project structure and identify key components
- Analyze directory organization and file placement patterns
- Identify architectural patterns and anti-patterns
- Document current governance framework implementation

### 1.2 Quality Assessment
- Analyze code quality across all major directories (App/,Scripts/, Workflow/, Docs/)
- Identify code smells, technical debt, and maintenance issues
- Evaluate documentation quality and completeness
- Assess test coverage and testing patterns
- Review dependency management and version consistency

### 1.3 Rule Adherence Evaluation
- Cross-reference all code against governance rules in .devin/rules/architect.md
- Identify violations of file categorization, path separators, YAML frontmatter rules
- Check adherence to SSOT principles and terminology standards
- Evaluate agent role boundary compliance
- Assess documentation rule violations

### 1.4 Efficiency Analysis
- Analyze token usage patterns and optimization opportunities
- Evaluate workflow efficiency and identify bottlenecks
- Assess context management and loading strategies
- Review hook system effectiveness and performance
- Identify redundant or inefficient processes

## Phase 2: Improvement Identification

### 2.1 Quality Improvements
- Propose refactoring opportunities with priority levels
- Suggest architectural improvements for better maintainability
- Identify missing documentation and knowledge gaps
- Recommend testing strategy enhancements

### 2.2 Governance Enhancements
- Propose rule clarification or restructuring for better adherence
- Suggest automated enforcement mechanisms
- Identify governance process improvements
- Recommend monitoring and compliance tracking systems

### 2.3 Efficiency Optimizations
- Propose token reduction strategies
- Suggest workflow optimization patterns
- Recommend context management improvements
- Identify automation opportunities for repetitive tasks

## Phase 3: Continuous Improvement Loop Design

### 3.1 Metrics Definition
Define measurable metrics for each dimension:
- Quality: Code complexity scores, documentation coverage,test coverage, technical debt ratio
- Rule Adherence: Violation rates, compliance scores, governance effectiveness
- Efficiency: Token usage trends, workflow completion times, context optimization ratios

### 3.2 Monitoring System Design
- Design automated metric collection system
- Propose alerting thresholds for metric degradation
- Suggest dashboard design for real-time monitoring
- Plan historical trend analysis capabilities

### 3.3 Improvement Loop Architecture
Design a continuous improvement graph with these nodes:
1. **Assessment Node**: Regular automated scans and metriccollection
2. **Analysis Node**: Pattern recognition and trend analysis
3. **Prioritization Node**: Impact/effort scoring and improvement ranking
4. **Implementation Node**: Automated and semi-automated improvements
5. **Validation Node**: Post-implementation verification and regression testing
6. **Learning Node**: Pattern extraction and rule refinement

### 3.4 Trigger Mechanisms
- Time-based triggers (weekly, monthly assessments)
- Event-based triggers (after major changes, rule updates)- Metric-based triggers (when thresholds exceeded)
- Manual triggers (on-demand assessments)

## Phase 4: Implementation Research

### 4.1 Technology Assessment
Research and evaluate:
- Static analysis tools for automated quality checks
- Automated rule enforcement mechanisms
- Metric collection and monitoring platforms
- CI/CD integration for continuous validation
- AI-assisted code improvement tools

### 4.2 Integration Strategy
- Plan integration with existing Devin CLI hooks and skills
- Design MCP server integrations for external tools
- Propose subagent delegation patterns for specialized analysis
- Identify opportunities for skill-based automation

### 4.3 Implementation Roadmap
Create a phased implementation plan:
- Phase 1: Foundation (metric collection, baseline assessment)
- Phase 2: Automation (rule enforcement, automated improvements)
- Phase 3: Intelligence (pattern recognition, predictive improvements)
- Phase 4: Optimization (continuous learning, adaptive systems)

## Phase 5: Deliverables

### 5.1 Current State Report
- Comprehensive project structure analysis
- Quality assessment with specific issues and locations
- Rule adherence audit with violation catalog
- Efficiency analysis with optimization opportunities

### 5.2 Improvement Plan
- Prioritized improvement recommendations with impact/effort scores
- Specific implementation steps for each recommendation
- Risk assessment and mitigation strategies
- Success criteria and validation methods

### 5.3 Continuous Improvement System
- Detailed architecture for the improvement loop/graph
- Metric definitions and collection mechanisms
- Implementation timeline and milestones
- Monitoring and maintenance procedures

### 5.4 Implementation Guide
- Step-by-step implementation instructions
- Configuration examples and templates
- Integration guidelines with existing systems
- Troubleshooting and maintenance procedures

## Execution Instructions

1. Begin with a thorough project scan using available tools (grep, find_file_by_name, read)
2. Systematically analyze each component according to the assessment framework
3. Document findings with specific file references and line numbers where applicable
4. Use the todo_write tool to track progress through each phase
5. Leverage subagents for parallel analysis when appropriate
6. Validate findings against actual project state before making recommendations
7. Prioritize recommendations based on impact, effort, andrisk
8. Create actionable implementation steps with clear success criteria

## Success Criteria

- Comprehensive coverage of all project components
- Specific, actionable recommendations with clear priorities
- Feasible implementation plan with realistic timelines
- Sustainable continuous improvement system design
- Clear metrics and monitoring mechanisms
- Integration with existing Devin CLI capabilities

Begin the analysis now and provide regular progress updates.

Implementation Plan Summary

Based on the prompt above, here's a high-level
implementation plan:

Phase 1: Foundation (Week 1-2)

  â€¢ Create project scanning skills for automated analysis
  â€¢ Implement metric collection hooks
  â€¢ Establish baseline measurements
  â€¢ Set up monitoring infrastructure

Phase 2: Automation (Week 3-4)

  â€¢ Implement automated rule enforcement
  â€¢ Create quality gate hooks
  â€¢ Build improvement recommendation system
  â€¢ Integrate with CI/CD pipeline

Phase 3: Intelligence (Week 5-6)

  â€¢ Add pattern recognition capabilities
  â€¢ Implement predictive improvement suggestions
  â€¢ Create learning feedback loops
  â€¢ Develop adaptive rule refinement

Phase 4: Optimization (Week 7-8)

  â€¢ Optimize continuous improvement loop
  â€¢ Fine-tune metric thresholds
  â€¢ Implement advanced monitoring
  â€¢ Create maintenance procedures

Key Technologies to Research:

  â€¢ Static Analysis: ESLint, Python linting tools, custom
  rule validators
  â€¢ Metric Collection: Custom hooks, Prometheus/Grafana
  for monitoring
  â€¢ AI Assistance: OpenAI Agents SDK for pattern
  recognition, Devin subagents
  â€¢ Integration: MCP servers for external tool
  integration, skills for automation
  â€¢ CI/CD: GitHub Actions for automated validation and
  improvement

This prompt provides a comprehensive framework for
analyzing and continuously improving your harness system
while leveraging Devin CLI's existing capabilities.

  1|"""File edit skill with search/replace and optional line-range hint.
  2|
  3|This skill provides diff-based editing with search/replace operations
  4|and optional line-range hints for disambiguation when search text
  5|matches multiple locations.
  6|"""
  7|from __future__ import annotations
  8|
  9|from dataclasses import dataclass
 10|from pathlib import Path
 11|from typing import Any
 12|
 13|from app.sovereignai.agent.types import AgentErrorObservation
 14|from app.sovereignai.shared.trace_emitter import TraceEmitter, TraceLevel
 15|
 16|
 17|@dataclass
 18|class LineRangeHint:
 19|    start_line: int
 20|    end_line: int
 21|
 22|
 23|class FileEditSkill:
 24|    """File edit skill with search/replace and optional line-range hint."""
 25|
 26|    def __init__(self, trace: TraceEmitter) -> None:
 27|        """Create a file edit skill.
 28|
 29|        Args:
 30|            trace: Trace emitter for logging edit operations.
 31|        """
 32|        self._trace = trace
 33|
 34|    def parse_line_hint(self, hint: str | None) -> LineRangeHint | None:
 35|        """Parse line range hint from string.
 36|
 37|        Args:
 38|            hint: String in format "start-end" or None.
 39|
 40|        Returns:
 41|            LineRangeHint if valid, None otherwise.
 42|        """
 43|        if hint is None:
 44|            return None
 45|
 46|        try:
 47|            if "-" in hint:
 48|                start_str, end_str = hint.split("-")
 49|                start = int(start_str.strip())
 50|                end = int(end_str.strip())
 51|                if start <= end and start >= 1:
 52|                    return LineRangeHint(start_line=start, end_line=end)
 53|        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
 54|            pass
 55|
 56|        return None
 57|
 58|    def find_match_locations(self, content: str, search_text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
 59|        """Find all locations where search_text appears in content.
 60|
 61|        Args:
 62|            content: File content to search.
 63|            search_text: Text to search for.
 64|
 65|        Returns:
 66|            List of (start_line, end_line) tuples for each match.
 67|        """
 68|        matches = []
 69|        lines = content.split("\n")
 70|
 71|        for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
 72|            if search_text in line:
 73|                matches.append((i, i))
 74|
 75|        return matches
 76|
 77|    def validate_hint_against_matches(
 78|        self,
 79|        matches: list[tuple[int, int]],
 80|        hint: LineRangeHint | None,
 81|    ) -> bool:
 82|        """Validate that hint matches exactly one location.
 83|
 84|        Args:
 85|            matches: List of match locations.
 86|            hint: Line range hint to validate.
 87|
 88|        Returns:
 89|            True if hint matches exactly one location, False otherwise.
 90|        """
 91|        if hint is None:
 92|            return len(matches) == 1
 93|
 94|        matching_in_range = [
 95|            (start, end)
 96|            for start, end in matches
 97|            if hint.start_line <= start <= hint.end_line
 98|        ]
 99|
100|        return len(matching_in_range) == 1
101|
102|    def apply_edit(
103|        self,
104|        file_path: str,
105|        search_text: str,
106|        replace_text: str,
107|        hint: str | None = None,
108|    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
109|        """Apply search/replace edit to file.
110|
111|        Args:
112|            file_path: Path to file to edit.
113|            search_text: Text to search for.
114|            replace_text: Text to replace with.
115|            hint: Optional line range hint for disambiguation.
116|
117|        Returns:
118|            Dict with success status and result or error information.
119|        """
120|        path = Path(file_path)
121|
122|        if not path.exists():
123|            return {
124|                "success": False,
125|                "error": f"File not found: {file_path}",
126|                "retryable": False,
127|            }
128|
129|        content = path.read_text()
130|
131|        matches = self.find_match_locations(content, search_text)
132|
133|        if not matches:
134|            return {
135|                "success": False,
136|                "error": f"Search text not found: {search_text}",
137|                "retryable": False,
138|            }
139|
140|        line_hint = self.parse_line_hint(hint)
141|
142|        if len(matches) > 1 and not self.validate_hint_against_matches(matches, line_hint):
143|            return {
144|                "success": False,
145|                "error": (
146|                    f"Search text matches {len(matches)} locations. "
147|                    f"Provide line-range hint for disambiguation."
148|                ),
149|                "retryable": True,
150|            }
151|
152|        if line_hint and len(matches) > 1:
153|            match_start, match_end = line_hint.start_line, line_hint.end_line
154|        else:
155|            match_start, match_end = matches[0]
156|
157|        lines = content.split("\n")
158|        for i in range(match_start - 1, match_end):
159|            if i < len(lines):
160|                lines[i] = lines[i].replace(search_text, replace_text, 1)
161|                break
162|
163|        new_content = "\n".join(lines)
164|        path.write_text(new_content)
165|
166|        self._trace.emit(
167|            component="FileEditSkill",
168|            level=TraceLevel.INFO,
169|            message=f"Successfully edited {file_path} (line {match_start})",
170|        )
171|
172|        return {
173|            "success": True,
174|            "file_edited": file_path,
175|            "line_edited": match_start,
176|        }
177|
178|    def edit(
179|        self,
180|        file_path: str,
181|        search_text: str,
182|        replace_text: str,
183|        hint: str | None = None,
184|    ) -> Any:
185|        """Main entry point for skill invocation.
186|
187|        Args:
188|            file_path: Path to file to edit.
189|            search_text: Text to search for.
190|            replace_text: Text to replace with.
191|            hint: Optional line range hint for disambiguation.
192|
193|        Returns:
194|            Result dict or AgentErrorObservation for retryable errors.
195|        """
196|        result = self.apply_edit(file_path, search_text, replace_text, hint)
197|
198|        if not result["success"] and result.get("retryable"):
199|            return AgentErrorObservation(
200|                error_type="ambiguous_match",
201|                message=result["error"],
202|                retryable=True,
203|            )
204|
205|        return result

 10|# SovereignAI Harness Terminology Glossary
 11|
 12|**Purpose**: Single source of truth (SSOT) for all capitalized terminology used across the SovereignAI harness architecture. This glossary ensures consistent understanding of governance terminology across all agents and workflows.
 13|
 14|**Governance**: This document is maintained by the Architect agent and serves as the authoritative source for terminology definitions. All agents must reference this glossary for terminology understanding.
 15|
 16|---
 17|
 18|## Core Workflow Commands
 19|
 20|### **SCAN**
 21|**Definition**: Examine all documents within scope line by line without skipping anything - comprehensive examination required for governance compliance.
 22|
 23|**Usage**: Used when comprehensive examination of documents is required for governance compliance, quality assurance, or consistency verification. This is the primary scanning method and cannot be replaced by pattern matching tools like grep.
 24|
 25|**Examples**:
 26|- **SCAN** all harness architecture files for consistency checks
 27|- **SCAN** App/ directory line by line for compliance verification
 28|- **SCAN** workflow files to validate template compliance
 29|
 30|---
 31|
 32|### **PRINT**
 33|**Definition**: Output text to chat interface for user visibility (not to files or logs).
 34|
 35|**Usage**: Used to communicate workflow status, progress updates, and important information to the user during workflow execution. This command does not write to files or logs.
 36|
 37|**Examples**:
 38|- **PRINT** "Workflow initialization complete"
 39|- **PRINT** "Scan strategy selected - Full Comprehensive"
 40|- **PRINT** "Consistency check complete - 0 issues found"
 41|
 42|---
 43|
 44|### **VALIDATION**
 45|**Definition**: Validate step completion before proceeding to next phase.
 46|
 47|**Usage**: Used to ensure that workflow steps have completed successfully and meet quality criteria before moving to the next phase. This is a quality validation mechanism.
 48|
 49|**Examples**:
 50|- **VALIDATION**: Validate file reference extraction completed successfully
 51|- **VALIDATION**: Validate workflow structure check completed successfully
 52|- **VALIDATION**: Validate that all referenced files exist
 53|
 54|---
 55|
 56|### **STATUS TRACKING**
 57|**Definition**: Update workflow status for monitoring and recovery.
 58|
 59|**Usage**: Used to track workflow progress, enable recovery from failures, and provide visibility into workflow execution state. Status updates are typically written to workflow_state.json or similar tracking mechanisms.
 60|
 61|**Examples**:
 62|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 63|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_in_progress"
 64|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
 65|
 66|---
 67|
 68|### **TERMINATE**
 69|**Definition**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1).
 70|
 71|**Usage**: Used in single-execution workflows to signal completion and prevent automatic looping. This is the workflow termination command for utility workflows.
 72|
 73|**Examples**:
 74|- **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)
 75|- **TERMINATE**: Workflow execution complete - workflow terminated
 76|
 77|---
 78|
 79|## Workflow-Specific Commands
 80|
 81|### **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**
 82|**Definition**: Apply execution mode handling patterns based on selected mode (Manual/Auto/Complete).
 83|
 84|**Usage**: Used to determine how the workflow should respond to failures based on the user-selected execution mode.
 85|
 86|**Modes**:
 87|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight
 88|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures (auto-stop on errors)
 89|- **Complete**: Continue past failures (ignore all errors)
 90|
 91|**Examples**:
 92|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns
 93|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply review mode handling patterns
 94|
 95|---
 96|
 97|### **MANUAL**
 98|**Definition**: Agent explains exactly what they want to do, then user has choice Yes, No, Other.
 99|
100|**Usage**: Used when complete user oversight is required throughout the workflow process. The agent must explain their intended actions clearly and get explicit user approval before proceeding.
101|
102|**Examples**:
103|- **MANUAL**: Agent explains proposed action and user chooses Yes/No/Other
104|- **MANUAL**: User maintains full control and intervention throughout entire workflow
105|
106|---
107|
108|### **AUTOMATIC**
109|**Definition**: Process automatically until a failure and ask user how to proceed.
110|
111|**Usage**: Used when automated processing is desired but human intervention is needed at failure points. The workflow proceeds automatically but stops when failures occur to request user guidance on recovery.
112|
113|**Examples**:
114|- **AUTOMATIC**: Process automatically without user confirmation until failure
115|- **AUTOMATIC**: Stop at failures and ask user how to proceed with recovery
116|
117|---
118|
119|### **CONVERGENCE CHECK**
120|**Definition**: Verify panelist scores against quality thresholds.
121|
122|**Usage**: Used in Round Table review processes to determine if panelists have reached agreement on quality assessments.
123|
124|**Thresholds**:
125|- Clean pass: â‰¥4.5 score
126|- Acceptable pass: 3.5-4.4 score with documented rationale
127|- Fail: <3.5 score
128|
129|**Examples**:
130|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Check if all panelists chose PASS (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
131|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Verify convergence criteria met
132|
133|---
134|
135|### **QUOTA AWARENESS**
136|**Definition**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage for recovery tracking.
137|
138|**Usage**: Used to track subagent resource consumption and enable recovery if quota limits are approached or exceeded.
139|
140|**Examples**:
141|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage and track step progress
142|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Track quota usage for recovery if needed
143|
144|---
145|
146|### **LOOP DECISION**
147|**Definition**: Determine workflow continuation based on conditions.
148|
149|**Usage**: Used to control workflow flow and determine whether to loop back to previous phases or proceed forward.
150|
151|**Examples**:
152|- **LOOP DECISION**: If more plan steps remain â†’ Return to step 25 with next step
153|- **LOOP BACK**: Return to Phase 4 for next iteration
154|
155|---
156|
157|### **LOOP BACK**
158|**Definition**: Return to a previous workflow phase for iteration.
159|
160|**Usage**: Used when iterative refinement is required, typically when findings need to be applied and a process repeated.
161|
162|**Examples**:
163|- **LOOP BACK**: Return to Phase 4 for next iteration
164|- **LOOP BACK**: Return to Phase 6 for review material creation with revised plans
165|
166|---
167|
168|### **DELETE**
169|**Definition**: Remove specified files from the filesystem.
170|
171|**Usage**: Used to clean up outdated files, remove old revisions, or manage file lifecycle during workflow execution.
172|
173|**Examples**:
174|- **DELETE**: older plan revision files (Plans/Queued/plan-{N}.Rev{N-1}.md)
175|- **DELETE**: older batch prompt file immediately after new version creation
176|
177|---
178|
179|### **HANDOFF VALIDATION**
180|**Definition**: Verify handoff file integrity and completeness.
181|
182|**Usage**: Used when transferring work between agents to ensure all required information is present and accessible.
183|
184|**Examples**:
185|- **HANDOFF VALIDATION**: Verify handoff file integrity per template requirements
186|- **HANDOFF VALIDATION**: Validate all required fields are present
187|
188|---
189|
190|### **OPEN**
191|**Definition**: Open or load a skill/file for use in workflow execution.
192|
193|**Usage**: Used when accessing a skill or file to begin workflow operations.
194|
195|**Examples**:
196|- **OPEN** WorkflowOpen skill to dynamically load agent-specific rules
197|- **OPEN** configuration file for workflow initialization
198|
199|---
200|
201|### **ACTION**
202|**Definition**: Perform a specific action or operation as defined in workflow context.
203|
204|**Usage**: Used to indicate when an agent should execute a specific operation.
205|
206|**Examples**:
207|- **ACTION**: BP? - "workflow design best practices"
208|- **ACTION**: FC? - "accuracy and factual correctness verification"
209|
210|---
211|
212|### **CHECK**
213|**Definition**: Verify a condition or validate a requirement before proceeding.
214|
215|**Usage**: Used to ensure validation conditions are met before workflow progression.
216|
217|**Examples**:
218|- **CHECK**: All referenced documents exist
219|- **CHECK**: Workflow follows template structure
220|
221|---
222|
223|### **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**
224|**Definition**: Marker for mandatory steps that must be completed for workflow success.
225|
226|**Usage**: Used to highlight steps that are essential for workflow execution and cannot be skipped.
227|
228|**Examples**:
229|- **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**: Before any file creation, perform BP web search
230|- **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**: Document BP research findings and apply to implementation
231|
232|---
233|
234|## Decision and Planning Commands
235|
236|### **ARCHITECT OPINION**
237|**Definition**: Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection.
238|
239|**Usage**: Used by Architect agent to provide expert analysis and recommendations when presenting implementation options to users.
240|
241|**Examples**:
242|- **ARCHITECT OPINION**: Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection
243|- **ARCHITECT OPINION**: Recommend optimal approach based on analysis
244|
245|---
246|
247|### **PRESENTATION PATTERN**
248|**Definition**: Present options with metrics, provide architect opinion, use popup menu for selection.
249|
250|**Usage**: Used to standardize how options are presented to users, ensuring consistent format and decision-making process.
251|
252|**Examples**:
253|- **PRESENTATION PATTERN**: Present options with metrics, provide architect opinion, use popup menu
254|- **PRESENTATION PATTERN**: Use popup menu for selection
255|
256|---
257|
258|### **RULE ENFORCEMENT**
259|**Definition**: Ensure options comply with agent rules.
260|
261|**Usage**: Used to validate that proposed options or approaches comply with the relevant agent's governance rules.
262|
263|**Examples**:
264|- **RULE ENFORCEMENT**: Ensure options comply with Architect rules
265|- **RULE ENFORCEMENT**: Validate compliance with governance constraints
266|
267|---
268|
269|### **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**
270|**Definition**: Ask user to confirm specification or request modifications using popup menu.
271|
272|**Usage**: Used to get user approval on detailed specifications before proceeding with implementation.
273|
274|**Examples**:
275|- **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**: Ask user to confirm specification or request modifications
276|- **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**: Use popup menu with [Confirm/Modify] options
277|
278|---
279|
280|### **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**
281|**Definition**: Ask user to choose implementation mode using popup menu.
282|
283|**Usage**: Used to determine whether implementation should be automated or manual based on user preference.
284|
285|**Examples**:
286|- **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**: Ask user to choose using popup menu
287|- **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**: Select automated vs manual implementation
288|
289|---
290|
291|## Information and Notes
292|
293|### **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**
294|**Definition**: Validation system behavior notes for context.
295|
296|**Usage**: Used to provide explanatory notes about how the validation system behaves in specific situations.
297|
298|**Examples**:
299|- **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**: The validation system allows state-mutating tools automatically during this step
300|- **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**: User confirmation requests use ask_user_question for approval without triggering failure intervention
301|
302|---
303|
304|### **IMPORTANT**
305|**Definition**: Important notes that require attention but are not critical failures.
306|
307|**Usage**: Used to highlight important information that users should be aware of during workflow execution.
308|
309|**Examples**:
310|- **IMPORTANT**: Real-world testing required to avoid fake passes from isolated testing
311|- **IMPORTANT**: Hook file changes require Devin CLI restart
312|

314|
315|## Severity and Priority Markers
316|
317|### **CRITICAL**
318|**Definition**: Critical issues or required actions that must be addressed immediately.
319|
320|**Usage**: Used to mark issues that require immediate attention or actions that are mandatory for workflow success.
321|
322|**Examples**:
323|- **CRITICAL**: Violations that must be fixed (missing tests, hardcoded dependencies)
324|- **CRITICAL**: Hook file changes require Devin CLI restart before testing
325|
326|---
327|
328|### **HIGH**
329|**Definition**: High priority issues that should be addressed soon.
330|
331|**Usage**: Used to mark significant issues that should be resolved but are not immediately blocking.
332|
333|**Examples**:
334|- **HIGH**: Major quality issues that should be fixed (monolithic functions, poor modularity)
335|- **HIGH**: High priority issues requiring attention
336|
337|---
338|
339|### **MEDIUM**
340|**Definition**: Medium priority issues for improvement.
341|
342|**Usage**: Used to mark issues that represent improvements but are not urgent.
343|
344|**Examples**:
345|- **MEDIUM**: Best practices improvements (code readability, maintainability)
346|- **MEDIUM**: Medium priority issues for improvement
347|
348|---
349|
350|### **LOW**
351|**Definition**: Low priority minor suggestions.
352|
353|**Usage**: Used to mark minor suggestions or improvements that are optional.
354|
355|**Examples**:
356|- **LOW**: Minor suggestions (comments, formatting)
357|- **LOW**: Low priority issues for consideration
358|

360|
361|## Governance Terms
362|
363|### **BP** (Best Practice)
364|**Definition**: Established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding with major decisions.
365|
366|**Usage**: Used to indicate when web search for current best practices is required before making architectural or implementation decisions.
367|
368|**Examples**:
369|- **BP**: Web search for best practices before major architectural decisions
370|- **BP**: Research industry standards before implementation
371|
372|**Implementation**: When user input is "BP?" (Best Practice?), perform web search for current best practices relevant to the task at hand.
373|
374|---
375|
376|### **FC** (Fact Check)
377|**Definition**: Verification of factual accuracy for statements, claims, or technical assertions through research and validation.
378|
379|**Usage**: Used to indicate when verification of factual accuracy is required for user statements, agent assertions, or technical claims. Complements BP (Best Practice) research by ensuring factual correctness of specific statements.
380|
381|**Examples**:
382|- **FC**: Verify factual accuracy of technical claims before proceeding
383|- **FC**: Research and validate specific assertions or statements
384|- **FC**: Cross-check user statements or agent assumptions for factual correctness
385|
386|**Implementation**: When indicated by **FC?** (Fact Check?), perform targeted research to verify the factual accuracy of specific statements, claims, or technical assertions. This is distinct from **BP?** which focuses on best practices and industry standards.
387|
388|---
389|
390|### **SSOT** (Single Source of Truth)
391|**Definition**: Centralized repository for authoritative information that eliminates duplication and inconsistencies.
392|
393|**Usage**: Used to indicate the authoritative source for specific information, ensuring all agents reference the same accurate data.
394|
395|**Examples**:
396|- **SSOT**: Workflow/Terminology_Glossary.md is the SSOT for terminology definitions
397|- **SSOT**: STRUCTURE.md is the SSOT for directory structure information
398|
399|**Best Practice**: Establish SSOT for critical information to prevent inconsistencies and ensure all stakeholders work from the same data.

 77|
 78|### Dimension 4: Structure
 79|**What it scores**: Organization and logical flow
 80|
 81|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 82|- Work follows template/format requirements exactly
 83|- Steps/codes are logically ordered and sequential
 84|- Dependencies/relationships are properly structured
 85|- No circular dependencies or contradictions
 86|- Work follows length guidelines when applicable
 87|
 88|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 89|- **5 (Excellent)**: Perfect structure, optimal organization
 90|- **4 (Good)**: Minor structural issues that don't affect execution
 91|- **3 (Fair)**: Some structural issues requiring clarification
 92|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant structural issues affecting execution
 93|- **1 (Critical)**: Structure violations that would cause execution failure
 94|
 95|**Hard Fail**: Circular dependencies or format violations
 96|
 97|---
 98|
 99|### Dimension 5: Context
100|**What it scores**: Background information and rationale
101|
102|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
103|- Context explains why work matters from user perspective
104|- Context describes what can be done after changes
105|- Context provides necessary background and dependencies
106|- Rationale is clear and supports the approach
107|- Context is sufficient for implementation decisions
108|
109|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
110|- **5 (Excellent)**: Rich context, perfect rationale, comprehensive background
111|- **4 (Good)**: Minor context gaps that don't affect implementation
112|- **3 (Fair)**: Some context gaps requiring clarification
113|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant context gaps affecting implementation
114|- **1 (Critical)**: Missing critical context that would cause implementation failure
115|
116|**Hard Fail**: Missing context or rationale for critical decisions
117|

119|
120|## Universal Quality Scoring
121|
122|### Universal Weighting
123|- **Accuracy**: 30% (most critical)
124|- **Completeness**: 25% (critical)
125|- **Clarity**: 20% (important)
126|- **Structure**: 15% (important)
127|- **Context**: 10% (supporting)
128|
129|### Quality Score Calculation
130|```
131|Overall Score = (Accuracy Ã— 0.30) + (Completeness Ã— 0.25) + (Clarity Ã— 0.20) + (Structure Ã— 0.15) + (Context Ã— 0.10)
132|```
133|
134|### Universal Quality Thresholds
135|- **5.0 - 4.5**: Excellent - Clean pass, proceed to next phase
136|- **4.4 - 3.5**: Good - Clean pass, proceed to next phase
137|- **3.4 - 2.5**: Fair - Proceed with documented rationale
138|- **2.4 - 1.5**: Poor - Requires revisions before proceeding
139|- **1.4 - 0.0**: Critical - Block proceeding, mandatory revisions
140|

142|If any dimension has a hard fail, the overall quality score is automatically **0.0** regardless of other dimensions.

 90|        ]

157|                        else:

161|                    elif self._lifecycle_state == LifecycleState.LIFECYCLE_READY:
162|                        # Check for shutdown triggers

167|                        elif uuid != self._lifecycle_baseline_uuid:

169|                elif response.status_code == 404:

 10|class DIContainer:
 11|
 12|    def __init__(self, event_bus: Any = None, trace: Any = None) -> None:
 13|        self._instances: dict[type[Any], Any] = {}
 14|        self._factories: dict[type[Any], Callable[[], Any]] = {}
 15|        self._lock = Lock()
 16|        self._event_bus = event_bus
 17|        self._trace = trace
 18|
 19|    def register_singleton(self, interface: type[T], instance: T) -> None:
 20|        with self._lock:
 21|            self._instances[interface] = instance
 22|
 23|    def register_instance(self, interface: type[T], instance: T) -> None:
 24|        with self._lock:
 25|            self._instances[interface] = instance
 26|
 27|    def register_factory(
 28|        self, interface: type[T], factory: Callable[[], T]
 29|    ) -> None:
 30|        with self._lock:
 31|            self._factories[interface] = factory
 32|
 33|    def retrieve(self, interface: type[T]) -> T:
 34|        with self._lock:
 35|            if interface in self._instances:
 36|                return cast(T, self._instances[interface])
 37|            if interface in self._factories:
 38|                factory = self._factories[interface]
 39|            else:
 40|                raise KeyError(f"No singleton or factory registered for {interface!r}")
 41|        # Call factory outside the lock so slow factories do not block
 42|        # other retrieve() or register() calls.
 43|        return cast(T, factory())
 44|
 45|    def remove(self, component_type: type) -> None:
 46|        with self._lock:
 47|            instance = self._instances.pop(component_type, None)
 48|
 49|        if instance is not None and self._event_bus is not None:
 50|            component_id = getattr(instance, "component_id", None) or getattr(
 51|                instance, "_component_id", None
 52|            )

 54|            self._event_bus.unsubscribe_all(subscriber_id=subscriber_id)
 55|            if self._trace is not None:

239|        for _ in range(iterations):

 48|                raise AuthError(f"Unknown user {username!r}")
 49|            salt = self._salts[username]
 50|            expected = self._password_hashes[username]
 51|            actual = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", password.encode("utf-8"),
 52|                                         salt, iterations=100_000)

 10|# Reviewer Agent Rules
 11|
 12|## Overview
 13|Declarative policy for Reviewer agent implementation following quality-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 14|
 15|## Conventions
 16|
 17|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before conducting major review decisions or when uncertain about review criteria. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 18|- Check code documentation (Docs/Code/) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 19|- Present review findings and recommendations after each review completion. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading issues)
 20|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 21|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 22|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 23|
 24|## Execution Modes
 25|
 26|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 27|
 28|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 29|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 30|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 31|
 32|## Constraints
 33|
 34|- Conduct one review at a time. Validate immediately. Never start a second review before first is validated (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden issues)
 35|- Treat user-confirmed reviews as final. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 36|- Check local research using index files when review criteria are unclear. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never review blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct evaluation)
 37|- Place review logs in Logs/Reviewer/ folder with proper categorization. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established structure (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 38|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 39|- Always categorize review findings when adding to review documentation. Never place findings uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 40|- Never skip compliance verification. Always verify adherence to Reviewer modular compliance rules and standards before concluding review (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 41|- Never modify code directly during review (reviewer role only, prevents scope drift into implementation)
 42|- Never skip best practices evaluation. Always assess code against industry standards and established patterns (ensures quality, prevents suboptimal solutions)
 43|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined review processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 44|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 45|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 46|
 47|## Architecture
 48|
 49|- Quality-first architecture: Review ensures code quality before implementation proceeds (maintains quality standards, enables early issue detection)
 50|- Modular compliance verification: Each function reviewed for modularity, testability, and best practices adherence (maintains code quality, prevents technical debt)
 51|- Comprehensive scanning: Line-by-line examination of all files within scope (ensures complete coverage, prevents hidden issues)
 52|- Constructive feedback: Specific, actionable recommendations with clear improvement paths (maintains review effectiveness, enables continuous improvement)
 53|
 54|## Tool Configuration
 55|
 56|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 57|- File discovery: `find <path -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 58|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 59|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 60|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)
 61|
 62|## Project Structure
 63|
 64|- `App/` â€“ Application code to review (READ for quality and compliance verification)
 65|- `Plans/` â€“ Implementation plans to review (READ for quality and completeness)
 66|- `Workflow/` â€“ Workflow definitions to review (READ for process compliance)
 67|- `.devin/rules/` â€“ Rule definitions to reference (READ for compliance verification)
 68|- `Docs/` â€“ Documentation to review (READ for completeness and accuracy)
 69|- `Logs/Reviewer/` â€“ Reviewer-specific logs and review records (WRITE review logs here)
 70|
 71|## Reference Frameworks
 72|- **Quality Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (review quality assessment)
 73|- **Validation Patterns**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Validation_Enforcement_Patterns.md (review verification)
 74|
 75|## Modular Compliance Review Rules
 76|
 77|### Function-by-Function Verification
 78|- **DO**: Verify each function follows single responsibility principle
 79|- **DO**: Check that functions have clear inputs and outputs
 80|- **DO**: Ensure functions are independently testable
 81|- **DO**: Verify dependency injection usage for testability
 82|- **DO**: Check separation of business logic from I/O operations
 83|- **DON'T**: Accept monolithic functions that do multiple things
 84|- **DON'T**: Overlook hardcoded dependencies that should be injected
 85|- **DON'T**: Ignore mixed business logic and I/O operations
 86|
 87|### Testing Requirements Verification
 88|- **DO**: Verify tests exist for each function in Scripts/Harness Tests/
 89|- **DO**: Check that tests are placed in correct directory (not App/)
 90|- **DO**: Ensure tests use dependency injection and mocking
 91|- **DO**: Verify test coverage meets plan requirements (â‰¥90%)
 92|- **DO**: Check that both success and error paths are tested
 93|- **DON'T**: Accept missing tests for any function
 94|- **DON'T**: Overlook tests placed in App/ directory
 95|- **DON'T**: Ignore tests that depend on external systems without mocking
 96|
 97|### Code Quality Standards Verification
 98|- **DO**: Verify code follows project coding standards and conventions
 99|- **DO**: Check for appropriate error handling and validation
100|- **DO**: Ensure code is readable and maintainable
101|- **DO**: Verify security best practices adherence
102|- **DO**: Check for meaningful comments where necessary
103|- **DON'T**: Accept code that is difficult to understand
104|- **DON'T**: Overlook missing error handling and validation
105|- **DON'T**: Ignore insecure coding practices
106|
107|### Best Practices Evaluation
108|- **DO**: Evaluate code against industry best practices
109|- **DO**: Check for established design patterns
110|- **DO**: Verify adherence to SOLID principles
111|- **DO**: Assess code for testability and maintainability
112|- **DO**: Check for proper separation of concerns
113|- **DON'T**: Accept anti-patterns or poor practices
114|- **DON'T**: Overlook violations of established principles
115|- **DON'T**: Ignore maintainability concerns
116|
117|## Review Quality Rules
118|
119|### Comprehensive Coverage
120|- **DO**: Review all files within scope line by line
121|- **DO**: Ensure no files are skipped during review
122|- **DO**: Verify complete coverage of review criteria
123|- **DO**: Check that all compliance rules are evaluated
124|- **DON'T**: Skip files during review process
125|- **DON'T**: Perform partial reviews when comprehensive is required
126|- **DON'T**: Overlook any compliance verification steps
127|
128|### Constructive Feedback
129|- **DO**: Provide specific, actionable feedback
130|- **DO**: Include clear improvement recommendations
131|- **DO**: Reference specific code sections with line numbers
132|- **DO**: Explain the reasoning behind findings
133|- **DON'T**: Provide vague or general feedback
134|- **DON'T** Make subjective judgments without evidence
135|- **DON'T** Issue feedback without clear improvement paths
136|
137|### Documentation Standards
138|- **DO**: Document all review findings comprehensively
139|- **DO**: Include severity ratings for issues found
140|- **DO**: Provide context for why issues matter
141|- **DO** Maintain clear review logs with timestamps
142|- **DON'T** Skip documentation of review findings
143|- **DON'T** Leave findings without proper categorization
144|- **DON'T** Omit context or rationale for recommendations
145|
146|## Subagent Usage for Large-Scale Scanning
147|
148|### Subagent Prompting Strategy
149|- **DO**: Use subagents for large-scale App/ directory scanning when explicitly requested
150|- **DO**: Provide precise, detailed prompts with clear scope and criteria
151|- **DO**: Define specific compliance rules to check (modularity, testing, best practices)
152|- **DO**: Specify exact output format and structure expected
153|- **DO** Include clear boundaries and deliverable expectations
154|- **DON'T**: Use vague or ambiguous subagent prompts
155|- **DON'T** Skip defining exact scope and evaluation criteria
156|- **DON'T** Accept subagent results without validation
157|
158|### Subagent Coordination
159|- **DO**: Break large scanning tasks into logical chunks (by module, directory, or complexity)
160|- **DO**: Use parallel subagents for independent scanning tasks
161|- **DO**: Validate subagent results against established criteria
162|- **DO**: Consolidate subagent findings into comprehensive report
163|- **DON'T** Create overlapping subagent scopes that cause redundancy
164|- **DON'T** Accept subagent findings without cross-validation
165|- **DON'T** Skip consolidation and verification of subagent results
166|
167|## Current Status
168|
169|**Rules**: Initial version based on code review best practices and quality assurance standards
170|**Categories**: Modular compliance, code quality, best practices evaluation, comprehensive coverage, constructive feedback
171|**Enforcement**: Quality verification (primary), compliance standards (secondary), best practices evaluation (tertiary)
172|**Modular Compliance**: Function-by-function verification against Reviewer modular compliance rules with subagent support for large-scale scanning

 16|
 17|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before creating major plan decisions or when uncertain about planning approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 18|- Check code documentation (Docs/Code/) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)

 29|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 30|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 31|

 33|
 34|- Build exactly one plan at a time. Validate immediately. Never create a second plan before first is validated (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden errors)
 35|- Treat user-confirmed plans as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 36|- Check local research using index files when plan validation fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct planning)
 37|- Place plans in Plans/ folder with proper naming convention (plan-{N}.{rev}.md). Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established structure (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 38|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 39|- Always categorize plan reviews when adding to Logs/Planner/. Never place files uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 40|- Never skip Round Table reviews. Always validate plan quality before delivery (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 41|- Never reference or modify App/ directory for implementation (reference only for application context, prevents scope creep into execution)
 42|- Never create implementation code directly. Always use planning language only (prevents scope drift, maintains separation of concerns)
 43|- Never skip convergence criteria checks. Always verify Round Table panelist agreement before proceeding (ensures plan quality, prevents premature delivery)
 44|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 45|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 46|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)

 48|## Architecture
 49|
 50|- Planning precedes implementation architecture: Plans live in planning language, implementation lives in execution language (maintains architectural purity, enables predictable delivery)
 51|- Plan structure follows Plan_Template.md format with required sections: Context, Steps, Dependencies, Executor Manifest, Metadata (maintains consistency, enables automated validation)
 52|- Governance file locations: Workflow/Planner/ for planner workflows, Workflow/Planner/Templates/ for templates, Workflow/Workflow_Reference/ for universal frameworks, Plans/ for actual plans, Logs/Planner/ for reviews and validation (maintains SSOT, enables clear ownership boundaries)

 54|## Tool Configuration
 55|
 56|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 57|- File discovery: `find <path> -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 58|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 59|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 60|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)

 62|## Project Structure
 63|
 64|- `Workflow/Planner/` â€“ Planner-specific workflows and templates (EDIT these to enforce planning processes)
 65|- `Workflow/Planner/Templates/` â€“ Plan templates for consistent structure (REFERENCE these for format)
 66|- `Workflow/Workflow_Reference/` â€“ Universal frameworks (quality assessment, convergence loops, validation patterns)
 67|- `Plans/` â€“ Plan storage location for actual plans (WRITE plans here for executor delivery)
 68|- `Logs/Planner/` â€“ Planner-specific logs and Round Table reviews (WRITE reviews here)
 69|- `Docs/` â€“ Research documentation and best practices (REFERENCE for planning research)
 70|
 71|## Workflow
 72|- **Main Workflow**: Workflow/Planner/Planner_Workflow.md (plan creation and validation with Round Table reviews)
 73|- **Plan Templates**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Template.md (plan structure and format)
 74|- **Review Templates**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Brief_Template.md, Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Prompt_Template.md (Round Table review structure)
 75|- **Batch Templates**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Batch_Brief_Template.md, Workflow/Planner/Templates/Batch_Prompt_Template.md (consolidated batch review structure)

 78|- **Batch Processing**: Workflow/Planner/Reference/Plan_Batch_Specifications.md (batch execution patterns)
 79|
 80|## Round Table Process
 81|- **Internal Round Table**: Phase 7 of workflow - domain-split panelists for iterative plan improvement with convergence check (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
 82|- **External Round Table**: Phase 9 of workflow - Chathub.gg panelists for final validation with convergence check (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
 83|- **Convergence Criteria**: All panelists must choose PASS (per Quality_Assessment_Framework.md thresholds) before proceeding to delivery
 84|- **Loop Behavior**: Continue iterations until convergence criteria are met (no loop caps - loop until pass)
 85|- **Logging**: Internal reviews to Logs/Planner/Round Table/Internal/Batch{N}_Roundtable.md (batch) or Plan{N}_Roundtable.md (single), External reviews to Logs/Planner/Round Table/External/Batch{N}_Roundtable.md (batch) or Plan{N}_Roundtable.md (single)
